findings.where: First screen, the action row: the filled blue 'Write to me' button and the underlined address 'Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com' beside it (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The page's one action looks like a button and a link but does nothing. The parts map lists 'Write to me' and the underlined address as static. The only working mailto is the small address in the footer at the very bottom of the page.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who has decided to contact Mark. They click the button or the address on the first screen and nothing happens, so the page fails at its one job (brand sheet §1).

findings.where: First screen, the 'Book a consultation' button beside 'Write to me' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: A second filled blue button, with the same weight, shape and colour as 'Write to me', so the first screen has two primary actions. It offers a booking service that neither the brief nor the brand sheet mentions. It links to #consult, and no consultation section appears anywhere in the parts map.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brief asks for one direct, personal way to reach Mark and one action on the first screen. A visitor also has to choose between two equal buttons, and one of them leads nowhere and suggests a sales funnel instead of a personal advisor.

findings.where: First screen, the first-person paragraph 'I advise multilateral development banks…' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: Mark's main self-introduction is set as four to eight lines of bold, widely tracked, all-capital sans. It is slow to read, it reads as a shouted label instead of his voice, and it is styled unlike the serif paragraph directly below it, which is the same kind of text.
findings.who_objects: A reader trying to learn what Mark does: this paragraph answers that question, and it is the hardest text on the page to read. The founder would object too, since the brief bans tracked, techy capitals and asks for Mark heard in the first person.

findings.where: First screen ground: the band behind the hero, shading from pale blue to lavender and pink (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The hero sits on a blue-to-lavender gradient, while the rest of the page and the tile's own palette declare a flat warm paper with three colours and no accent. The lavender-pink is outside both house colours, and the gradient reads as a generic, slick tech-landing look rather than a legal journal.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brief asks for the house blue and grey only, a warm paper ground, and nothing slick or techy. The palette section below also contradicts what the visitor has just seen.

findings.where: First screen margin notes ('Istanbul, 2025 / Best Practices in PPP Legislation…', 'Melbourne, 2026…', 'São Paulo, 2024…'); also the blue section labels below (Palette, Type, Texture, Article page, Motion, Tile notes)
findings.fault: The talk titles are set in the house blue, which the tile's own palette assigns to links and the action, yet they are static. They look like links to the talks and lead nowhere.
findings.who_objects: A procurement reader who wants to check Mark's talk in Istanbul or Melbourne. They click the title expecting the talk or its slides, get nothing, and lose the evidence that would build trust.

findings.where: Phone first screen, the action row
findings.fault: 'Book a consultation' is indented off the text column and wedged under the address's underline. The three action parts stack raggedly instead of on one left edge.
findings.who_objects: A phone visitor. The cluster looks broken at the moment they are meant to act, which undercuts the 'refined' impression the brief asks for.

findings.where: Header: the arch mark with 'MMM INFRA' on the left, then the name 'Mark M. Moseley' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The logo comes first and the name second. On desktop, the 'MMM INFRA' lettering sits right on the top edge of the hero band, so the lockup looks clipped.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brief says his name leads with the logo beside it. A clipped lockup also looks unfinished to a first visitor.

findings.fault: There is no Contact item in the navigation. Apart from the dead hero button, the only way to reach Mark is the footer address.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who arrives deep in the page, or who comes back later to write to Mark, looks to the navigation for Contact and finds no such item.

findings.where: Exhibit photograph in the hero and in the motion sketch
findings.fault: The framed photo is a static part with a wide, soft drop shadow, which reads as a floating or clickable card. Its flat greyscale grade also makes Mark look like an archive or obituary image rather than a real person in real light.
findings.who_objects: A first visitor, who may read the lifted photo as something to click. The founder asked for photos graded into the house colours and for Mark to be seen warmly, and this grade makes him look cold and distant.

findings.where: Article specimen: the document row's outlined pill 'Download' button, compared with the hero's square-cornered filled buttons
findings.fault: The page's two actions take unrelated shapes, a rounded capsule here and sharp rectangles in the hero, with no reason in function.
findings.who_objects: Angélique and later page builders, who need one action style to reuse. Visitors also see two vocabularies on one site.

findings.where: Article specimen: the gap between 'With a new PPP Act, the country can:' and its three-item list
findings.fault: The lead-in sentence is cut off from its list by a full paragraph gap, as large as the gap between unrelated paragraphs. Proximity therefore splits a sentence from its own continuation, which is the rhythm test the brief set for Angélique's content.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked that the type rhythm hold when a list is added. Readers also see the list as detached from the sentence it completes.

findings.where: Desktop motion sketch: the curve on the left and the exhibit photo far right, set lower
findings.fault: The curve and the photo it animates sit far apart, at different heights, with a large empty block under the curve, so they do not read as one demonstration.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who reviews the motion sketch. The link between the timing curve and the moving element is lost.
